summary: Onboarding and tooling session between Angelo, who runs sales operations, and Andrew Musial, a brand-new closer roughly three weeks into the role who has not yet closed a deal. Angelo screen-shares through the Close CRM inbox — clearing reminders, tasks and inherited SMS threads, reassigning opportunities from the previous rep Harry so they appear in Andrew's pipeline, and merging a duplicate lead record so the application data attaches to the right contact. They then cover how outbound texting works for international leads, since the dialler blocks non-US numbers and WhatsApp is the workaround. Andrew raises two policy questions: whether payments can be split, having seen Harry close a deal that way on a recorded call, and how he will be paid, which leads into setting up Gusto against his Polish LLC.
notable: Payment-plan policy stated and immediately qualified. Angelo on a 3K-now-3K-over-90-days split: 'No, that's not generally an option that we offer.' He then confirmed a two-pay does exist — 'a toupee is payment 1 today, payment 2 in 30 days' — and, told that Harry had closed a deal on the 90-day version, replied 'Well, that's interesting. I'll, I'll check in on him with that' and 'That's Harry being a little creative.'

Improvisation on price was explicitly sanctioned to new reps: 'if you're on a call and you need to get creative, worst case, you try to make something work. I get it, you know, especially on your first couple of calls, like, you know, if we need to get the deal through'.

Stated no-show policy. A call the rep missed because of his own double-booking is logged against the prospect: 'technically, you know, we still count it as a no-show. I mean, they maybe didn't no-show us, but like, at the end of the day, the call didn't happen.'

SalesKit is described as an AI bot that messages leads hands-off: 'It's designed to be hands-off, or you don't need to go and message people.' No mention of whether leads are told they are talking to automation.

Andrew Musial had taken over calls originally booked for Harry Edmonds when Harry could not take them, and inherited transferred leads from a previous salesperson, which means folder attribution does not reliably indicate who owned the lead.

Timeline context for the rest of this batch: Andrew is new enough that 'May 1st, I wasn't here', calls himself 'very new to close', and Angelo tells him 'you're going to knock your first deal down soon' — so every sales call in this batch predates his first close.

Andrew is paid as a contractor through Gusto against a Polish LLC, with Angelo unsure whether international direct deposit works: 'I'm most 99% sure. Again, it could be a little different with, you know, Poland.'

CRM data quality is poor by both parties' account — duplicate leads for the same prospect with different phone numbers, a number that 'didn't get formatted properly and put like a one in front of it', and stray messages neither man could explain: 'I don't know why this got sent.'
